title: Why Do Chatbots Always Say '7'? The Secret Groupthink Problem in AI
summary: Try this: ask ChatGPT or Claude for a random number between 1 and 10. I bet it said 7. Ask again, maybe 3 or 4. It's like magic, but it's actually a big problem. Most AI chatbots are super predictable. They give the same answers over and over, even when you want fresh ideas. This is called 'groupthink.' It's fine for math, but what if you're brainstorming a band name or a vacation spot? You don't want the same old thing everyone else gets. An Australian startup called Springboards noticed this and built a new AI model named Flint. Flint is trained to be more creative. When the CEO, Pip Bingemann, asked three models for a car type, ChatGPT and Claude said Toyota or Honda. Flint said Ford F-150. For a New Balance shoe slogan, the first two said 'Run your way.' Flint said 'Built to last, run to win.' Why does this happen? Researchers think it's because most AI models learn from similar data in similar ways. They all end up thinking alike—like a class where everyone copies the same homework. Flint mixes things up on purpose. It's like having a friend who always suggests the weird, cool idea you'd never think of. Springboards hopes Flint will help people in advertising and design break out of boring patterns. So next time you need a spark of creativity, maybe don't trust the bot that always says 7.
why_it_matters: If you ever need a truly original idea, don't just trust the first answer a bot gives—remember, its '7' might not be the best number for you.

keywords.explanation: Chatbots are computer programs that talk to you like a real person, often to answer questions or help with tasks.
Groupthink is when everyone in a group (or even an AI) thinks the same way and no one suggests new ideas.
Predictable means you can guess what will happen next because it always happens the same way.
Brainstorming is coming up with lots of ideas quickly, without judging them at first, to find something original.
A startup is a young company that tries to bring a new product or service to the world.
A slogan is a short, memorable phrase used in ads to make people remember a product.

background_read: AI chatbots like ChatGPT (made by the company OpenAI) and Claude (made by Anthropic) have been trained on billions of web pages, so they often repeat the most common ideas.
The Australian startup Springboards created a new AI named Flint that deliberately tries to 'think outside the box,' which helps people in jobs like advertising.
Psychologists use the word 'groupthink' to describe when groups go along with the crowd—and now the same thing happens inside computer brains.
Article_Structure: WHO: Springboards, an Australian startup, and its CEO Pip Bingemann.
WHAT: A problem where AI chatbots give the same predictable answers (groupthink), and a new model named Flint that is trained to be more creative.
WHERE: The story comes from Australia, where the startup is based.
WHY: To help people in creative fields like advertising break out of boring patterns and discover original ideas.

perspectives.description: Advertisers and designers welcome Flint because it helps them brainstorm fresh slogans and product names that stand out from the crowd.
Some teachers worry that AI groupthink could mean students all get the same easy answers, making it harder to learn to think for themselves.
Tech experts see this as a design flaw in how AI learns from past data, and they are working on ways to make machines more inventive.
